summary.title: Typography for Lawyers
summary.one_liner: A book by Matthew Butterick that teaches lawyers practical typography rules for type composition, font choice, page layout, and legal document samples.
keywords: how to embed fonts in a word document
takeaways: Legal documents benefit from deliberate typographic choices in punctuation, spacing, and quotation marks.
Font recommendations include Equity, Valkyrie, Century Supra, Concourse, and others, with alternatives for common system fonts.
Page layout rules cover line spacing, line length, margins, block quotes, lists, tables, footnotes, and widow/orphan control.
Sample documents such as caption pages, motions, memos, letterhead, and contracts show the rules applied.
The appendix covers how to make a PDF and how to embed fonts in a Word document.
summary.summary: This is the table-of-contents-style summary page for Matthew Butterick's book Typography for Lawyers. The page outlines the book's structure: type composition rules (quotes, dashes, spacing, ligatures), text formatting, font recommendations with alternatives to common system fonts, and page layout guidance. It also includes sample legal documents such as motions, memos, and contracts, plus an appendix on making PDFs and embedding fonts.
